items.stem: Write the balanced equation for the reaction of sodium carbonate with dilute nitric acid. How will you test the gas evolved?

items.stem: Write the balanced equation for the reaction of hydrochloric acid with sodium hydroxide and name the salt formed.
items.answer: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O; salt: sodium chloride

items.stem: 12 mL of a sodium hydroxide solution is exactly neutralised by 8 mL of a given hydrochloric acid solution. How much of the same acid is needed to neutralise 24 mL of the same NaOH solution?
items.answer: 16 mL

items.stem: Write the balanced equation for the reaction of iron with dilute hydrochloric acid and name the gas evolved.

items.markingKey: 1 mark: Dilution – the process of decreasing the concentration of ions per unit volume by adding water to an acid or a base.

items.stem: 12 mL of a sodium hydroxide solution is exactly neutralised by 9 mL of a given hydrochloric acid solution. How much of the same acid is needed to neutralise 18 mL of the same NaOH solution?
items.markingKey: Acid needed is proportional to the base: 9 × 18/12 = 13.5 mL.
